item.title: PTAD unveils N5bn health scheme, announces N180bn pension payments
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young LAGOS — The Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) has unveiled a N5 billion health insurance scheme for retirees under the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS), while announcing over N180 billion in pension-related payments and interventions in the last two years. The Executive Secretary of PTAD, Tolulope Odunaiya, disclosed this on Thursday at a stakeholder engagement forum in Lagos, where she outlined the Directorate’s achievements in pension administration, including the settlement of inherited pension liabilities, payment of pension increment arrears and introduction of digital reforms to improve service delivery. Odunaiya said the N5 billion intervention culminated in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS pensioners, which was formally unveiled at the event. “Most significantly, we secured funding of approximately N5 billion for a major healthcare intervention, culminating in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS Pensioners, which we are unveiling today,” she said. She explained that the scheme was designed to address retirees’ healthcare needs, stressing that their welfare extended beyond the regular payment of monthly pensions. “This initiative reflects our recognition that Pensioners’ welfare extends beyond the timely payment of monthly pension entitlements. Access to free, quality, and reliable healthcare is fundamental to their well-being and quality of life,” she added. On pension liabilities, the Executive Secretary disclosed that PTAD had settled over N91.5 billion in inherited obligations, including N25.05 billion paid to 9,675 former employees of the defunct Nigerian Telecommunications Limited (NITEL) and its mobile subsidiary, MTEL, as final settlement of outstanding entitlements. She also said over N60 billion had been paid in arrears arising from the N32,000 pension increment, benefiting more than 150,000 eligible pensioners. In addition, the Directorate paid over N23.8 billion in arrears arising from pension increments of 10.66 per cent, 12.95 per cent, 13.8 per cent and 20.55 per cent, alongside the implementation of corresponding increases in monthly pensions. On pension harmonisation, Odunaiya said PTAD had disbursed over N5 billion in arrears to more than 64,000 eligible pensioners. She added that over 30,000 pensioners had benefited from monthly pension re-computation, with N3.8 billion paid in associated arrears. The Executive Secretary further announced that 726 retirees had been enrolled on the pension payroll, comprising 508 former employees of the Federal Mortgage Finance Limited (FMFL) and 218 retirees of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN). The new beneficiaries attract a combined monthly pension obligation of over N41 million, she said. item.title: ‘Completely unacceptable’: Kimmich blasts Bayern over Musiala treatment
item.description: Bayern Munich vice-captain Joshua Kimmich has hit out at the club’s hierarchy for pressuring Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Speaking after a Champions League defeat at Lille on Wednesday, the Germany skipper — who is Bayern’s captain with Manuel Neuer currently injured — became the latest to criticise the German giants. “Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than the players, but it is not bigger than the person,” Kimmich said. “It’s completely unacceptable and is not the Bayern way… What’s happening now is something that must not happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.” In August, Musiala collapsed twice on the field in pre-season games and then revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Musiala played last Friday in his first match since a two-month absence with an unrelated hamstring injury. Moments after the match, long-time club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge said the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form and should accept a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Honorary president Uli Hoeness and current club chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen have made similar statements. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension in February 2025. According to German media reports, he earns 25 million euros ($27 million) per season, making Musiala the club’s second-highest paid player after Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. On Sunday, international players’ union FIFPRO accused Bayern of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. Kimmich said he understood the club’s position but was critical of the decision to go public. “I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal’s agent or with Jamal himself,” Kimmich said. Kimmich missed several games in October after the sudden death of his father and said he appreciated the support of the club during that time. “In my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out,” Kimmich added. Wednesday’s defeat to Lille ended Bayern’s run as the last club in Europe’s top-five leagues yet to suffer defeat in any competition. item.title: Lagos govt, UNICEF, NGE seek action on child welfare
item.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh LAGOS — The Lagos State Government, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) and other stakeholders have called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The call was made on Thursday at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, themed: “Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility.” The event was organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME), with participation from Airtel Nigeria and other stakeholders. Speaking at the symposium, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, said ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential was a collective responsibility that should not be left to government alone. Citing a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, Anaba described the figure as alarming and called for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to assess their contributions towards addressing the challenge. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms Lone Hvass, said Nigeria’s future would be determined by the decisions made today to protect and invest in its children. She said child survival, education and learning were interconnected, noting that children excluded from school were also denied opportunities for protection, participation and the realisation of their potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said the welfare of children required sustained commitment from government, parents, caregivers, development partners and the media. item.title: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 5 (Full list)
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe, Sporting CP striker Luis Suarez and Como attacker Anastasios Douvikas are jointly leading the UEFA Champions League scoring chart after the conclusion of Matchday 5. The trio have each scored six goals in the competition this season, maintaining a narrow lead over a group of players who have found the net five times. Mbappe strengthened his position with a brace in Real Madrid’s 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday. Suarez also scored twice in Sporting CP’s 2-2 draw against Manchester United, taking his tally to six goals, while Douvikas remains on the same number. Roma forward Donyell Malen, Manchester City’s Erling Haaland and Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi are next on the list with five goals each. Eight players are tied on four goals, including Paris Saint-Germain duo Ousmane Dembele and Fabian Ruiz, Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, Borussia Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane. The other players on four goals are Galatasaray’s Aleksey Batrakov, Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic and Barcelona forward Raphinha. The Champions League Golden Boot race remains open as the league phase continues, with several leading attackers still in contention. item.title: NANS hails FG’s move to manufacture passports
item.description: By Adeola Badru The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has described Nigeria’s move to manufacture its own international passports as a significant step towards ending foreign dependence in the production of a document central to the country’s national identity. The association said the establishment of the National Passport Manufacturing Centre (NPMC) would strengthen Nigeria’s sovereignty, while commending the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, for spearheading the initiative. NANS President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, stated this in a press release issued on Thursday, in which he also praised the minister’s reforms in the passport system and the Ministry of Interior. He described the centre as a historic achievement, noting that Nigeria had never manufactured its own international passports since gaining independence more than six decades ago. “More than six decades after Nigeria gained independence, this is the first time Nigeria will dare to produce her own passport. Under Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo as the Minister of Interior, Nigeria has taken ownership of a document that represents our identity as a sovereign nation for the first time in our nation’s history,” he said. The students’ body said the initiative, which followed several reforms in the passport system, represented a milestone in the country’s efforts to strengthen its national identity and improve public service delivery. It described the groundbreaking ceremony for the centre as a “grand and laudable achievement”, adding that the development reflected the minister’s commitment to nation-building. NANS also said Tunji-Ojo had changed perceptions about the Ministry of Interior, which it said was previously regarded by some as being largely preoccupied with the declaration of public holidays. “BTO has tremendously changed the narrative of the Ministry of Interior. For a ministry that was largely perceived by many as a ministry whose activities revolved around the declaration of public holidays, his leadership has brought a new face to the ministry,” the statement said. “Today, we have a working ministry delivering on its mandate beyond imagination. This is a remarkable shift that deserves recognition.” The association said reforms introduced in the passport system had also eased the difficulties Nigerians previously encountered in obtaining and renewing international passports. It noted that delays and bureaucratic bottlenecks had made the process difficult for many citizens, but said the minister had changed the situation within less than four years. “For years, Nigerians have had to contend with unnecessary delays, bottlenecks and difficulties in obtaining or renewing their international passports. “However, in less than four years, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo has changed the status quo, and the process is now a seamless one,” it said. Amupitan warned on Thursday as ‎ the Commission and security agencies meet to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 general election. ‎The INEC Chairman stressed the need for political actors to embrace issue-based campaigns, respect opposing views and conduct their political activities within the provisions of the law. item.title: DSS foils kidnap attempt in Lafia, arrests three suspects
item.description: By Soni Daniel Community leaders in Lafia Emirate, Lafia Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, have commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for foiling a kidnap attempt in the area and arresting three suspects in connection with the incident. The leaders praised the DSS operatives for their swift response to a distress call following an attempted abduction at the Isa Mustapha Agwai area of Lafia metropolis. Speaking on behalf of the community leaders, the Mai-angwa (community leader) of Farin Kasa community, Chief Yahaya Mohammed, described the operatives as dedicated and professional in the discharge of their duties. Mohammed said the security operatives arrived within minutes of receiving the distress call after unidentified gunmen invaded the community around midnight and attempted to abduct residents. “Some unidentified gunmen invaded our community and attempted to kidnap residents. We immediately alerted DSS operatives who swiftly arrived at the scene. The operatives exchanged gunfire with the abductors,” he said. He said the intervention had restored residents’ confidence in the security agencies, commending the collaboration between the DSS and other security outfits, including community vigilantes. He urged security agencies to ensure that all suspects arrested in connection with the incident were prosecuted in accordance with the law. Meanwhile, three suspects have been taken into DSS custody over the foiled attack. They were identified as Hassan Musa, 19; Muhammadu Sani Idris, 20; and Sale Umaru Zangba, 47. A source disclosed that Zangba, a cleaner at a primary healthcare centre in the area, allegedly confessed to treating one of the suspects who sustained gunshot injuries during the exchange of fire. The source said the DSS had sustained its operations against kidnapping, arms trafficking and other criminal activities in Nasarawa State. According to the source, the agency recorded another breakthrough about three weeks ago with the arrest of one Bello Abdullahi, a suspected arms courier allegedly on his way to deliver weapons to bandits in Kebbi State. The source also disclosed that a suspected kidnapper was arrested while allegedly collecting ransom from a female resident of Nasarawa State. The source assured that those arrested in connection with the various incidents would face the full weight of the law. item.title: Gunmen kill 16, injure four in overnight attack on Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos No fewer than 16 persons, including women, youths and children, have been killed after gunmen stormed Tafi Gana community, a hamlet of Kyie Ihwien, near Jebbu Miango in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attack, according to the Irigwe Development Association (IDA), occurred at about 11:30pm on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, leaving four other persons injured and throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. The association, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Sam Jugo, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Thursday, said, “The attackers wielded assault rifles and other dangerous weapons.” “They stormed the community and started shooting sporadically.” It added, “By dawn of Thursday, November 26, 2026, about 16 persons lay dead, while four other survivors were rushed to unknown medical facilities with various degrees of injuries.” The association gave the names of those killed as Moses Oko, 70; Maingwa Zere Rangya, 60; Danladi Ishaku, 45; Luka Danladi, 21; Elisha Luka, 18; David Danladi, 10; Ishaya Goslow, 18; Lami Danladi, 30; Isi Ishaku, 18; Zhime Ngaza, 75; ThankGod Danladi, 18; Gideon Joseph, 25; Ladi Abba, 65; Ruth Istifanus, 20; Mary Keyi, 18; and Lazarus Musa, 13. The statement quoted the traditional ruler of the area, Nggwe Gado Dama, as confirming the incident, adding that the matter had been reported to security agencies. It said, “The matter had been reported to security operatives who were, as at press time, at the scene of the attack.” The association condemned the killings and appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid taking the law into their hands. It said, “The IDA appeals to all natives not to take laws into their hands but allow the security agencies to do the needful to dispense justice to the slain.” The association expressed condolences to the bereaved families and the entire Irigwe nation, praying for the repose of the souls of the victims and God’s comfort for their immediate families. item.title: Mr Latin hands over TAMPAN presidency after eight years
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actor, Bolaji Amusan, popularly known as Mr Latin, has stepped down as president of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria (TAMPAN) after eight years in office. Amusan handed over the association’s leadership to his successor, Ajala Jalingo, at a transition ceremony, announcing the development in a post on his Instagram page on Wednesday. Sharing a video of the handover, the actor described the occasion as the end of his eight year tenure as the association’s Global President. “Today, I officially handed over the TAMPAN flag to my successor, @ajala_jalingo, bringing my eight-year tenure as Global President to a close,” he wrote. Amusan, who became president in December 2018 following the resignation of his predecessor, Dele Odule, was re-elected unopposed in December 2022 for another four-year term. Although he has left the presidency, the actor will remain involved in the association as a member of its Board of Trustees. “I bow out with gratitude, honour and fulfilment, while embracing a new responsibility as a distinguished member of the prestigious Board of Trustees (BOT) of TAMPAN,” he added. He also expressed confidence in the association’s future under Jalingo’s leadership, saying the change in administration would not affect its commitment to service and development. “Leadership may change, but commitment to service and the growth of TAMPAN remains unwavering,” Amusan said. TAMPAN represents theatre and film practitioners across Nigeria, particularly those in the Yoruba movie industry. The association works to promote members’ interests and welfare, as well as the development of the entertainment sector. Amusan began his acting career in 1988 and is known for his comic roles in Yoruba films. He has also worked as a filmmaker and producer. item.title: Mourners Mark Hong Kong Fire Anniversary, Authorities Warn Against ‘Disorder’
item.description: A stream of mourners laid flowers Thursday at the site of a horrific fire that ripped through a Hong Kong apartment complex and killed 168 people a year ago, with authorities warning against “acts of disorder”. The world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 began on the afternoon of November 26, 2025 and raged for two days, gutting seven of Wang Fuk Court’s eight high-rise buildings that were home to some 4,600 people. Authorities in the Chinese territory — where Beijing has cracked down on dissent — appear wary of commemorations taking on a political tone and plan no official memorial. Police on Thursday kept a low profile as mourners laid hundreds of bouquets at a small park beneath the charred shells of the ruined buildings. They included former residents who stood on the same spot a year ago desperately waiting for news of their loved ones. “Families are torn apart, and people died,” said Koey Tam, a housewife and former resident in her 40s who lost her home, adding that they “can never be compensated with a new flat and a huge sum of money”. Smoke rises from apartments after a major fire swept through several blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential estate in Hong Kong’s Tai Po district on November 27, 2025. (Photo by DALE DE LA REY / AFP) The government was “a bit cold” to hold no official memorials, she added. “What can a memorial event possibly affect?” Grace Chan, 69, expressed her frustration at what she called people’s “self-censorship”, telling reporters that “at first, I thought they’d given us a large space” to pay respects to the victims. “Too many Hongkongers remain silent,” she said, as she left a single chrysanthemum at the site. Former resident Dorz Cheung told AFP that he still felt “very, very, very angry” about the government’s response to oversights exposed in the tragedy. “There are still so many emotions… anger, deep sadness, they’re all around.” ‘Seeking Accountability’ A mourner brings flowers to Wang Fu Court in Hong Kong on November 26, 2026, the site of a horrific fire that ripped through seven apartment blocks and killed 168 people a year before. (Photo by Peter PARKS / AFP) The blaze was Hong Kong’s worst disaster in more than seven decades, and a shock to the 7.5 million residents of one of Asia’s safest cities. The city’s number two official Eric Chan said the government will offer help to “lawful” memorial events, but warned against “acts of disorder”. The Chinese government’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office spoke this week against attempts to “cause chaos” under the guise of commemorations. According to media reports, some local journalists have faced internal pressure when covering the fire, including to shelve programmes originally scheduled to go on air. A government spokesperson told AFP that as long as it is “within the law”, there are “no restrictions on the freedom to comment and criticise government policies for media outlets”. item.title: Musk says will give two SpaceX shares to ‘every child in America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. item.title: The Deposit Takes Seconds but Why Does the Withdrawal Take Days
item.description: When online, especially depositing money can feel almost effortless. When playing games online, a player chooses a payment method, enters their required details and they often see the funds appear in their account within a matter of seconds. When the time comes when the player wants to withdraw their money , it can be a very different experience. The request may remain pending for hours before additional processing and banking delays extend the wait across several days. That contrast naturally causes frustration. If a platform can accept money instantly, why can it not return money at the same speed. The answer involves more than payment technology. Withdrawals move through security checks, internal approval processes, payment providers, and banking systems that deposits may not encounter in the same way. Deposits and Withdrawals Are Not Mirror Images A deposit is designed to confirm that funds are available and can be transferred successfully. Payment networks can authorize many card and digital wallet transactions almost immediately. Once authorization is received, the casino can credit the player’s balance, even if the complete financial settlement happens later. A withdrawal requires the platform to release funds from its own system. Before doing so, the operator may need to confirm the player’s identity, verify account ownership, review transaction history, and check whether promotional conditions have been satisfied. The payment must then be approved and sent through an eligible withdrawal method. This difference means that an instant deposit does not prove that an instant withdrawal is technically or operationally possible. However, it also does not excuse operators that create unnecessary obstacles or fail to communicate their procedures clearly. Verification Can Become the First Bottleneck Identity verification is one of the most common reasons for a delayed withdrawal. Casinos may request proof of identity, proof of address, or evidence showing that the payment method belongs to the account holder. These checks are intended to reduce fraud, prevent unauthorized payments, and meet financial compliance obligations. Problems arise when verification is delayed until a player asks to withdraw. Someone may have deposited and played without interruption, only to discover that documents are required before any winnings can be released. Uploading those documents takes minutes, but manual review may take considerably longer, particularly during weekends or periods of high demand. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: US targets Africa’s critical minerals to counter rivals
item.description: In 2026, the United States went on an economic offensive looking to access critical minerals across Africa in its race to compete with China for materials that are essential for new technologies and the energy transformation. Will 2027 deliver on these promises for African governments and will the new Democrat-controlled US Congress complicate US deals with investigations into their transparency? – Investments or promises? – American companies and consortiums this year announced large-scale mining investment projects through partnerships in Guinea, South Africa, Mozambique and Kenya. But it was the strategic partnership agreed in December 2025 with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) that illustrated Washington’s economic push to secure its supply of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China. China has had a long head-start. It began investing in the African mining sector in the 1990s. The deal stipulated that Kinshasa would identify a portfolio of mining assets on which American investors have a right of first offer. In return, the Congolese government secured diplomatic support from Washington on security in its volatile eastern region, rocked by violence by myriad armed groups for more than 30 years. Since then, the American company Virtus Minerals, in partnership with the Indian group Lloyds Metals&Energy, has announced the acquisition of Chemaf, a heavily indebted Congolese company specialising in copper and cobalt. Orion Critical Mineral Consortium is negotiating with the international group Glencore for a 40-percent stake in its Mutanda and Kamoto mines, which also produce copper and cobalt. – Transparency probes? – Kinshasa urged Washington this month to “move from signed agreements to actual investments”. But the Democrats’ triumph in the US midterm elections could complicate the implementation of the partnerships concluded by the Trump administration amid questions about their transparency. The Democrats have already announced plans to open investigations early next year into the conditions under which the Trump administration conducted the negotiations. “Nothing should change in 2027 regarding the partnership principle, because the supply of minerals is of strategic national interest to the United States,” a mining source in the DRC told AFP. “The industry received bipartisan assurances on this issue in the run-up to the elections,” the source added. “But the agreements could be subject to opportunistic scrutiny by the Democrats, which might slow their implementation,” the source said. – Local economic benefits? – Several African countries have clearly demonstrated their determination to draw economic benefits from the partnerships. Zimbabwe suspended exports of raw minerals in February, ahead of a total ban in 2027, saying it would require processing and transformation to take place in the country. item.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. According to him, the weapons were returned to the plane, which Nigerian soldiers then surrounded to ensure they were not smuggled out later. item.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. item.title: 2027: ADC’s Babba Kaita Rallies Katsina Voters, Promises LG Autonomy, Anti-Corruption Drive
item.description: The Katsina State Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 general elections, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita, has described the forthcoming polls as a crucial battle that Nigerians must pursue with determination and collective strength. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. The statement said residents, including youths, women and community leaders, have continued to welcome the campaign team with prayers, endorsements and assurances of support as the party intensifies its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: New York Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade Over Major Storm
item.description: New York postponed the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday over fears of extreme weather, a first in the event’s 100-year history, as a major storm gathers steam on the US East Coast. The brewing “nor’easter” threatens to disrupt plans for millions of people hitting the road and flying around the Thursday holiday, one of the country’s busiest travel seasons. “With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s told AFP in a statement. A balloon of Buckaroo Bob The Minion rests under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP The date change has prompted questions about the thousands of parade participants, including musicians and technical staff, who had made arrangements for a Thursday parade. “Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday,” the company said. The annual parade sees brightly colored balloons travel some 2.5 miles (four kilometers) from Midtown Manhattan to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store on 34th Street. Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. It is the first time in its history that it has been postponed, The New York Post reported. ‘Heartbroken’ New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed press conference on November 25, 2026 in New York City. Manoli Figetakis/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Manoli Figetakis / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) “This will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour, with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a safety briefing Wednesday. “The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning as well as a coastal flood warning. “Winds will be strong enough (Thursday) to down tree limbs and power lines.” The worst of the storm will strike later Thursday when strong winds, heavy rain and the evening high tide will overlap, the city warned in a travel advisory. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade in 1997. Workers prepare a balloon under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP Volunteers struggled but failed to keep a tight rein on ropes which constantly threatened to slam into onlookers. The careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” — from the popular children’s book — toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious.
